_note: Facts list for LabelLie. Gemma reads the label; these entries supply the facts. Codes not listed here are explained by AI (Claude, or Gemma if no Claude key) and marked as AI answers. Check each entry against its source before the demo.

100.name: Curcumin (turmeric colour)
100.fact: Yellow colour from turmeric. Generally considered safe.

101.name: Riboflavin (vitamin B2)
101.fact: Vitamin B2, used as a yellow colour. Generally considered safe.

102.name: Tartrazine (yellow colour)
102.fact: In the EU, foods with this colour must carry a warning that it may affect activity and attention in children.

104.name: Quinoline Yellow (colour)
104.fact: In the EU, foods with this colour must carry a warning that it may affect activity and attention in children.

110.name: Sunset Yellow (colour)
110.fact: In the EU, foods with this colour must carry a warning that it may affect activity and attention in children.

120.name: Carmine / Cochineal (red colour)
120.fact: Red colour made from crushed cochineal insects, so it is not vegetarian. Rarely causes allergic reactions.

122.name: Carmoisine (red colour)
122.fact: In the EU, foods with this colour must carry a warning that it may affect activity and attention in children.

124.name: Ponceau 4R (red colour)
124.fact: In the EU, foods with this colour must carry a warning that it may affect activity and attention in children.

127.name: Erythrosine (pink-red colour)
127.fact: The EU allows it only in cocktail and candied cherries. The US FDA revoked its use in foods in 2025.

129.name: Allura Red (colour)
129.fact: In the EU, foods with this colour must carry a warning that it may affect activity and attention in children.

132.name: Indigo Carmine (blue colour)
132.fact: Synthetic blue colour. Permitted in India, the EU and the US without a warning label.

133.name: Brilliant Blue FCF (blue colour)
133.fact: Synthetic blue colour. Permitted in India, the EU and the US without a warning label.

140.name: Chlorophyll (green colour)
140.fact: Natural green colour from plants. Generally considered safe.

150a.name: Plain caramel
150a.fact: Brown colour made by heating sugar. Generally considered safe.

150c.name: Ammonia caramel
150c.fact: Brown colour. Permitted within daily limits.

150d.name: Sulphite ammonia caramel
150d.fact: Brown colour used in colas and sweets. Permitted; it contains small amounts of 4-MEI, which regulators monitor.

160a.name: Beta-carotene (orange colour)
160a.fact: The orange pigment found in carrots. Generally considered safe.

160b.name: Annatto (orange colour)
160b.fact: Orange colour from annatto seeds. Rarely causes allergic reactions.

160c.name: Paprika extract
160c.fact: Red-orange colour from paprika. Generally considered safe.

162.name: Beetroot red
162.fact: Red colour from beetroot. Generally considered safe.

163.name: Anthocyanins
163.fact: Purple-red colour from fruits and vegetables like grapes. Generally considered safe.

171.name: Titanium dioxide (white colour)
171.fact: No longer allowed as a food additive in the EU since 2022.

200.name: Sorbic acid
200.fact: Stops mould growth. Generally considered safe at permitted levels.

202.name: Potassium sorbate
202.fact: Stops mould growth. Generally considered safe at permitted levels.

211.name: Sodium benzoate
211.fact: Permitted, but together with vitamin C it can form small amounts of benzene, which regulators monitor in drinks.
211.source: US FDA, benzene in soft drinks

220.name: Sulphur dioxide (sulphite)
220.fact: A sulphite. It must be declared as an allergen in the EU and can trigger asthma in sensitive people.

223.name: Sodium metabisulphite (sulphite)
223.fact: A sulphite. It must be declared as an allergen in the EU and can trigger asthma in sensitive people.

296.name: Malic acid
296.fact: Gives a sour taste, found naturally in apples. Generally considered safe.

319.name: TBHQ
319.fact: Keeps oils from going rancid. Permitted only within strict daily limits.

320.name: BHA
320.fact: Permitted within limits. IARC lists it as possibly carcinogenic to humans (Group 2B).

321.name: BHT
321.fact: Keeps fats fresh. Permitted only within daily limits.

322.name: Lecithin
322.fact: Usually from soy or sunflower. Generally considered safe.

330.name: Citric acid
330.fact: Found naturally in lemons. Generally considered safe.

407.name: Carrageenan
407.fact: Thickener made from seaweed. Permitted in foods.

412.name: Guar gum
412.fact: Thickener from guar beans, a crop grown widely in India. Generally considered safe.

414.name: Gum arabic
414.fact: Natural gum from acacia trees, used in candy coatings. Generally considered safe.

415.name: Xanthan gum
415.fact: Thickener made by fermentation. Generally considered safe.

440.name: Pectin
440.fact: Natural gelling agent from fruit. Generally considered safe.

471.name: Mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids
471.fact: Makes oil and water mix. Can be made from plant or animal fat.

476.name: PGPR (polyglycerol polyricinoleate)
476.fact: Made from castor oil. Used in chocolate so it flows easily, often to reduce cocoa butter.

503.name: Ammonium bicarbonate
503.fact: Makes biscuits light and crisp. Generally considered safe.

542.name: Bone phosphate
542.fact: Made from animal bones, so it is not vegetarian.

621.name: MSG (Monosodium glutamate)
621.fact: Considered safe by food regulators at normal amounts; some people report mild sensitivity.

627.name: Disodium guanylate
627.fact: Boosts savoury taste, often used with MSG. Can be made from fish, meat or yeast.

631.name: Disodium inosinate
631.fact: Boosts savoury taste, often used with MSG. Can be made from fish, meat or plant sources.

635.name: Disodium ribonucleotides
635.fact: A mix of INS 627 and 631 used in instant noodles and chips. Source can be animal or plant.

901.name: Beeswax
901.fact: Wax made by bees, used to make sweets shiny.

903.name: Carnauba wax
903.fact: Wax from palm leaves that gives candy-coated chocolates their shine. Generally considered safe.

904.name: Shellac
904.fact: Shiny coating made from a resin secreted by lac insects. Permitted, but not vegan and avoided by some vegetarians.

924a.name: Potassium bromate
924a.fact: Banned in India by FSSAI in 2016 and not allowed in the EU.

950.name: Acesulfame potassium (sweetener)
950.fact: WHO advises against using non-sugar sweeteners for weight control.

951.name: Aspartame (sweetener)
951.fact: IARC classed it as 'possibly carcinogenic' (Group 2B) in 2023, while JECFA kept the safe daily limit unchanged. Not suitable for people with PKU.

955.name: Sucralose (sweetener)
955.fact: WHO advises against using non-sugar sweeteners for weight control.

1422.name: Acetylated distarch adipate (modified starch)
1422.fact: Starch changed to work better in sauces and fillings. Generally considered safe.

by_name.name: Maltodextrin
by_name.fact: A processed carb that raises blood sugar very fast, like sugar.

by_name.name: Sugar under another name
by_name.fact: This is a form of sugar. Brands split sugar into several names so it appears lower in the list.

by_name.name: Maida (refined wheat flour)
by_name.fact: 'Refined wheat flour' is maida, not whole wheat. Little fibre.

by_name.name: Hydrogenated fat
by_name.fact: A source of trans fat. WHO calls for removing industrial trans fat; FSSAI limits it to 2% in fats and oils.

by_name.name: Gelatin
by_name.fact: Made from animal skin and bones, so it is not vegetarian.

by_name.name: Added flavouring
by_name.fact: The taste comes from added flavour, not only from the real ingredient shown on the pack.
